# Directive 17

> We build companies that improve the human experience. The Future Should Make Life Better.

Directive 17 is a venture firm founded by Joel Shapiro. Every company begins with one question: how will this make someone's life better? Only then do we ask whether it can become a great business.

## Pages

- [Why We Exist](https://directive17.com/why.html): Most organizations begin with markets. We begin with people.
- [Philosophy](https://directive17.com/philosophy.html): The Five Pillars — happiness, health, trust, connection, human potential — and the Human Test.
- [Companies](https://directive17.com/companies.html): Portfolio companies. Different companies. One philosophy.
- [The Future We See](https://directive17.com/future.html): What future is worth building?
- [Build With Us](https://directive17.com/build.html): Contact — joel@directive17.com
- [A Note from the Founder](https://directive17.com/#founder-note): Joel Shapiro on why Directive 17 exists and what it invests in.

## Companies

- [Holonic](https://directive17.com/companies/holonic.html): Holonic Technologies is building the infrastructure that helps enterprises trust what their technology produces. Its deterministic and semantic validation layer is designed to verify that software and AI-generated changes meet defined business rules, preserve intended functionality, and satisfy operational requirements before they are accepted for use.
- [Firefly.love](https://directive17.com/companies/firefly-love.html): Firefly.love is developing a conversational archive of a person’s life, preserving their stories, voice, values, and experiences for the people closest to them. Guided interviews help individuals capture the memories and perspectives that can be difficult to record without a starting point. AI organizes that material into an archive that families can explore through conversation.
- [Twelve92](https://directive17.com/companies/twelve92.html): Twelve92 is not another private club. It is an entirely new category of hospitality—a private community and lifestyle platform designed to make life more extraordinary, more convenient, and infinitely more enjoyable.
- [HumanOS](https://directive17.com/companies/humanos.html): HumanOS is developing a physician-led health and longevity institution that brings diagnostics, mental well-being, movement, recovery, and nutrition into one coordinated setting. Its approach begins with understanding the individual through medical assessment, personal goals, and information gathered over time. Physicians and supporting specialists would use that understanding to shape a connected plan for care, daily habits, and physical and cognitive performance.
- [Vector](https://directive17.com/companies/vector.html): Vector is building a living, evidence-backed professional profile designed to replace the static résumé. It brings together the substance of a person’s work, the skills they develop, the responsibilities they take on, and the judgment they demonstrate. By following those changes over time, Vector creates a more complete picture of professional identity, including the direction, momentum, and trajectory of a person’s career.
- [Vertical Longevity Pharmaceuticals](https://directive17.com/companies/vertical-longevity-pharmaceuticals.html): Vertical Longevity Pharmaceuticals is developing a vaccine platform designed to help the immune system recognize and clear senescent cells associated with aging and chronic disease. Its lead candidate, VLP-1, uses virus-like particle technology to direct that immune response, with an initial research focus on atherosclerosis, the buildup of plaque in arteries.
- [Mythogenic](https://directive17.com/companies/mythogenic.html): Mythogenic is developing MythOS, a browser-based world builder that turns ideas, prompts, maps, and creative briefs into rich, editable 3D environments. Its applications span gaming, entertainment, film and cinema, as well as simulation and training. Creators can shape a world’s geography, structures, narrative, and rules within a shared environment that remains open to revision as the project develops.
- [Pivt](https://directive17.com/companies/pivt.html): Pivt helps employees build personal connections as they navigate relocation, new roles, and other career transitions. Its platform matches people with peers and trained buddies based on shared experiences, location, and professional circumstances. Guided conversations, community groups, and local connections give employees practical ways to establish a support network as they settle into unfamiliar surroundings.
- [Caviar & Corndogs](https://directive17.com/companies/caviar-and-corndogs.html): Caviar & Corndogs is a hospitality destination built around extraordinary food, everyday pleasures, discovery, and human connection. Planned for Atlanta’s South Buckhead neighborhood, the approximately 18,000-square-foot flagship brings together dining, a curated gourmet market, an in-house coffee roastery, a bakery, a chocolate room, exceptional wines and Champagne, and beautiful spaces to gather.
- [Colossal Laboratories & Biosciences](https://directive17.com/companies/colossal.html): Colossal develops biotechnology for de-extinction and species conservation, combining genetics, reproductive biology, and computational research. Its programs include efforts to restore characteristics of lost species such as the woolly mammoth, thylacine, and dodo, while developing the scientific tools needed to pursue those goals.
- [LARX](https://directive17.com/companies/larx.html): LARX brings imagery, video, sensor feeds, and operational information into a single intelligence platform. Using AI to interpret visual and spatial data, it helps analysts and decision-makers search across sources, understand changing conditions, and work from a shared view of an environment. Users can explore information through plain-language queries, making complex data more accessible across technical and operational teams.
- [Epirus](https://directive17.com/companies/epirus.html): Epirus develops directed-energy technology to defend against drones and coordinated autonomous attacks. Its Leonidas system uses high-power microwaves to disable drone electronics and is designed to engage multiple threats at once. Powered by electricity, the system supports repeated engagements as part of a broader defense around a protected site or asset.
- [General Fusion](https://directive17.com/companies/general-fusion.html): General Fusion is developing technology to make fusion energy a practical source of commercial electricity. Its Magnetized Target Fusion approach combines magnetized plasma, mechanical compression, and liquid metal systems. In the proposed power plant design, liquid metal would protect the machine and capture heat from the fusion reaction for conversion into electricity.
- [Advocate](https://directive17.com/companies/advocate.html): Advocate helps people whose medical conditions limit their ability to work navigate the Social Security disability benefits process. It combines technology with a dedicated support team to organize medical evidence, prepare applications, and guide applicants through the requirements of a claim. Disability specialists, clinical support staff, and case managers contribute to the process, helping people understand what is needed and what comes next.

## Joel's Blog

- [AI Can Write the Code. Who Checks Its Work?](https://directive17.com/blog/who-checks-its-work.html): AI can now write more software code in an afternoon than entire engineering teams could produce in months.
- [See a Problem. Find a Solution. Have the Proverbial “Balls” to Fix It!](https://directive17.com/blog/get-a-bigger-plate.html): Or, as my wife calls it: “What the fuck are you doing now?”
- [What is the Holonic backstory, learning how to turn my “Smart TV to a single channel, and becoming an AI expert in 24 months?](https://directive17.com/blog/the-holonic-backstory.html): I Asked One Simple Question. Two Years and a Few Million Dollars Later, I Think I Finally Understand the Answer.
- [Last One In Is a Rotten Egg!](https://directive17.com/blog/last-one-in-is-a-rotten-egg.html): Is there another investment firm on earth where every employee gets a text at 8 a.m. that says: “Last one in is a rotten egg!”
- [What Could Go Wrong? V2](https://directive17.com/blog/what-could-go-wrong-v2.html): A look back at yesterday’s food and beverage intake, a new toilet, and a whole lot of love.
- [He/She/It/Them/They/Cow/Dog/Sheep/WTFF](https://directive17.com/blog/he-she-it-them-they.html): A friend of mine WAS a waiter at a very high-end restaurant in Atlanta. I emphasize WAS.
- [A Funeral For A Grin](https://directive17.com/blog/a-funeral-for-a-grin.html): A very old friend of mine died a couple of years ago. I had lunch with him last week. So, overall, he seems to be doing much better.
- [Joel, You Are Going to Get Cancelled.](https://directive17.com/blog/you-are-going-to-get-cancelled.html): My Chief of Staff informs me I am in danger of being cancelled. My offense: I wrote that women’s poop stinks. Apparently this was controversial.
- [Changing the World, “One” Hat at a Time](https://directive17.com/blog/one-hat-at-a-time.html): A young pro golfer asked me to sponsor him on the PGA Tour. Everyone thought that was hilarious. So what exactly are we laughing at?
- [What Could Go Wrong?](https://directive17.com/blog/what-could-go-wrong.html): Aspen Birthday Party Edition — twelve middle-aged men, three days of aggressive dehydration, and a 14-mile hike at 12,500 feet. In the rain.
- [My Life Philosophy May Be Terrible Advice](https://directive17.com/blog/my-life-philosophy.html): A list of sayings that felt less like inspirational wisdom and more like somebody had been secretly following me around for decades taking notes.
- [Apple, Psyllium & the Complete Collapse of Western Civilization](https://directive17.com/blog/apple-psyllium.html): I bought a MacBook. At almost exactly the same time, in an entirely unrelated act of spectacularly bad judgment, I added psyllium to my diet.
- [Black Plastic](https://directive17.com/blog/black-plastic.html): A meal-prep place with a beautiful sourcing story, a nutrition person, and a transparency pitch — serving everything in black plastic.
- [I Trust AI. I'm Starting Not to Trust the People Using It.](https://directive17.com/blog/i-trust-ai.html): Most people are worried about whether they can trust artificial intelligence. I have a different concern.
- [I Haven't Even Taken Off Yet](https://directive17.com/blog/i-havent-even-taken-off-yet.html): Another travel day. More craziness. And, as I write this, the airplane hasn't even left the gate.
- [There Are Some Things We Were Never Meant to Know](https://directive17.com/blog/some-things-we-were-never-meant-to-know.html): I would like to address one of the great architectural mistakes of our time: the unisex restaurant bathroom.
- [Stop Watching. Start F@cking Creating.](https://directive17.com/blog/stop-watching-start-creating.html): At some point, we became a civilization of spectators. We have been handed superpowers and we are using them to watch strangers organize their refrigerators.
- [One Second. I'm Trying to Reach You.](https://directive17.com/blog/one-second-im-trying-to-reach-you.html): A true story about traffic, modern medicine, the Philippines, and humanity's relentless pursuit of efficiency.
- [We Have Run Out of Fish](https://directive17.com/blog/we-have-run-out-of-fish.html): One Quick Question — true stories from a world that makes less sense every day.
